case_title: Ranjeet Goswami v. State of Jharkhand & Anr.
evidence_type: Documentary (school leaving certificate and admission-register records) and oral evidence of the head mistress on age; no eyewitness, medical or recovery evidence on the alleged offences is described
mitigating_circumstances: The accused was held to be a juvenile on the date of occurrence
trial_court_outcome: JJ Board rejected the juvenility claim on 27.03.2009 and held the accused not a juvenile; no verdict on the charges is stated
high_court_outcome: Criminal Revision allowed; JJ Board order restored and Sessions Judge's order set aside
neutral_facts: The accused was charge-sheeted with offences relating to an incident that occurred on the night of 12/13 April 2008. The accused later surrendered. The judgment does not describe the circumstances of the alleged assault, the identity of the victim, or the manner of any death. The material placed before the court concerned the accused's age on the date of occurrence. A school leaving certificate issued on 10 April 2004 by the then principal of a primary school recorded the accused's date of birth as 10 May 1991. The head mistress of the school identified and recognised the principal's signature on that certificate and gave evidence to that effect. An investigating officer's report indicated that the accused and another person with a similar name were different persons. A medical board was separately asked to assess age and opined that the accused was about 20 years old on the date of occurrence.
key_evidence_accepted: School leaving certificate issued on 10.04.2004 showing date of birth 10.05.1991, proved through the head mistress's evidence identifying the principal's signature
witness_credibility: The head mistress's evidence was unchallenged and the Court accepted it; the Court also noted the investigating officer's report that the two named persons were different
post_offence_conduct: Surrendered on 13.06.2008 after the charge-sheet was submitted
trial_duration: offence: 12/13.04.2008; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 29.10.2010; Supreme Court: 18.09.2013
legal_representation: Accused: Shankar Narayanan (for Gaurav Agrawal). State and respondent: Jayesh Gaurav (for Gopal Prasad), Barun Kr. Sinha, Pratibha Sinha, Aayush Raj (for Rameshwar Prasad Goyal)
investigation_status: Charge-sheet filed; juvenility dispute raised before the JJ Board; case committed to Sessions Court and then directed to the JJ Board
procedural_irregularity: The High Court reversed the Sessions Judge without stating cogent reasons to discard the school leaving certificate
appeal_history: JJ Board: rejected juvenility claim (27.03.2009). Sessions Judge: set aside JJ Board order and directed trial by JJ Board. High Court: revision allowed, JJ Board order restored. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, High Court order set aside and Sessions Judge's order restored
prosecution_argument: The High Court rightly accepted the medical board report, which assessed the accused as about 20 years old on the date of occurrence, because of confusion over the documents produced
defence_argument: The High Court erred in reversing without examining the school admission register, which was properly proved through the head mistress; the medical board report could be considered only if the certificate was discarded for cogent reasons
legal_principle_applied: Where a school leaving certificate is proved and no cogent reason exists to reject it, juvenility is established from it and no medical examination is needed
precedent_relied_upon: Ashwani Kumar Saxena v. State of M.P. (2012) 9 SCC 750 (2012 (10) SCR 540)
other_sentence_order: Accused to be tried only by the Juvenile Justice Board
